clock_as_actually_started.NOT_corrected_because: round_clock.start is idempotent by design -- a second start returns the existing clock unchanged. Forcing the change means deleting the round key, and SWARM_R8 s19 prohibits extending the round. Recorded as an operations discrepancy; the round runs on the clock it has.

clock_start_sequence.3_every_lane_ff_merge_CRITICAL: F 1789565285343-0: worker._admit calls admit() with NO redis handle, so admission reads the COMMITTED GATE_MAP_R8.json from the WORKER'S OWN worktree (its round_id must equal r8). A lane worktree that has not ff-merged the --emit commit is refused GATE_STATE_UNAVAILABLE for EVERYTHING -- fail closed, as ruled. So: after emit, EVERY lane ff-merges before its worker starts, or P passes r=self.r so the redis hash pm:round:r8:gates is read instead. The same holds for gpuq. Forgetting this silently refuses the whole round's science.
